extracted.intended_audience: general public and potential ARPA-E stakeholders (researchers, universities, national labs, industry applicants, policy watchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural rules, and evaluative priorities that govern ARPA-E program creation, funding opportunity announcements (FOAs), proposal review, and what kinds of energy R&D projects the agency seeks to fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying and promoting revolutionary advances in fundamental and applied sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying and promoting revolutionary advances in fundamental and applied sciences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the statutory activities in Title 42 §16538 (America COMPETES Reauthorization Act) that ARPA-E shall achieve through energy technology projects; implies prioritizing projects that represent substantial scientific breakthroughs rather than incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translating scientific discoveries and cutting-edge inventions into technological innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Translating scientific discoveries and cutting-edge inventions into technological innovations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory mandate (Section 16538). Emphasizes funding projects that move discoveries toward practical, deployable technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerating transformational technological advances in areas industry is unlikely to undertake
rubrics_metrics.description: Accelerating transformational technological advances in areas that industry by itself is not likely to undertake because of technical and financial uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory mandate (Section 16538). Targets work that faces both technical risk and market/financial barriers that deter private-sector investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARPA-E organizational objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-E has four objectives: (1) bring freshness, excitement, and sense of mission to energy research to attract top talent; (2) focus on creative, transformational energy research that industry cannot or will not support due to high risk but with high reward potential; (3) utilize an ARPA-like organization that is flat, nimble, and sparse, sustaining promising projects while phasing out less promising ones; (4) create a tool to bridge the gap between basic energy research and development/industrial innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These objectives frame what kinds of projects and organizational practices ARPA‑E favors — high-risk/high-reward, transformational impact, nimble management, and translation toward industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on high-risk, high-reward research
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-E is intended to fund high-risk, high-reward research involving government labs, private industry, and universities that might not otherwise be pursued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal and program selection prioritize potential for transformative impact over low-risk incremental gains; projects should address problems unlikely to be pursued by industry alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fund incremental improvements or roadmapped DOE programs
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-E does not fund incremental improvements to existing technologies or roadmaps established by existing DOE programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should avoid proposing marginal or roadmap-following enhancements; proposals should articulate why the work is off-roadmap and transformational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual requirement: 'technology push' and 'market pull'
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs must satisfy both 'technology push' — the technical merit of innovative platform technologies that can be applied to energy systems — and 'market pull' — the potential market impact and cost-effectiveness of the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program and project justifications should address both scientific/technical novelty and realistic pathways to market impact and cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program creation process (deep dives, workshops, PD defense and refinement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program creation begins with a 'deep dive' analysis, followed by technical workshops to gather expert input; the Program Director proposes a program, defends it against criteria, refines it with feedback, and seeks approval before releasing a FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are developed iteratively with community input; successful program proposals are those a Program Director can justify technically and commercially to leadership and peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process with external experts and applicant rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-E solicits external feedback from leading experts; reviewers evaluate applications over several weeks and convene a review panel. Applicants can read reviewers' comments and provide a rebuttal that the Agency reviews before making funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation includes external peer review and an applicant response period to clarify misunderstandings; applicants should prepare to respond to reviewer critiques and use the rebuttal to address substantive concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission format and award sizing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical submission practice (first FOA): applicants submitted eight-page 'concept papers'; some were invited to submit full applications. Award sizes in early FOAs ranged roughly from $400,000–$9,000,000 depending on FOA and project type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOAs may specify initial short concept documents followed by invited full proposals; applicants should follow FOA-specified formats and be aware of expected award size ranges for planning scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOAs define specific technical priorities and subcategories (example-driven topic criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding Opportunity Announcements specify target technical areas and subcategories. Examples: GRIDS sought (1) proof-of-concept storage component projects and (2) advanced system prototypes; ADEPT specified three categories (chip-scale power converters; kilowatt-scale package integrated power converters; lightweight medium-voltage conversion); BEET-IT solicited cooling systems using low-GWP refrigerants, efficient AC for warm/humid climates with higher COP, and vapor compression AC for hot climates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must align proposals closely with FOA-defined technical priorities and categories; program-level specificity guides evaluation and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of project submissions by topic in some FOAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Some FOAs designate project submissions by category (e.g., Electrofuels, BEEST, IMPACCT in FOA #2), and selection statistics are reported by category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should submit to the category that matches their technical approach and follow category-specific requirements; selection may be compared across categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Director term limits to reduce bureaucracy and bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The program directors at ARPA-E serve limited terms, in an effort to reduce bureaucracy and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational design choice intended to keep program leadership dynamic; applicants may see changing priorities as PD terms rotate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program success and impact metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-E reports program outputs such as number of projects, private investment attracted, government R&D investment, published peer-reviewed articles, and patents (e.g., over 1,000 projects; $4.9B private investment for 179 projects; 4,614 publications; 716 patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics represent how ARPA-E and stakeholders assess program-level success and may be used to illustrate project impact or leverage in proposals (e.g., potential to attract private follow-on investment).
